def: An improver that is itself among the things it is allowed to change, and that raises a score of its own performance.
A program that takes a solution and a utility and returns a better solution, such as a search loop that proposes edits and keeps the ones that score higher.
A function that turns a solution into a number so that two solutions can be compared.
The score of an improver: the mean utility of the solutions it produces over a set of training tasks.
The idea that a system whose gains make it better at producing further gains could compound, which every published system bounds by its search space, judge, budget and frozen model.
Schmidhuber's design for a system that rewrites any part of itself, including its proof searcher, but only after proving the rewrite raises its expected reward.
The part of a Gödel machine that looks for a formal proof that a particular self-rewrite will help.
A method from Zelikman and colleagues in which a language-model-based improver rewrites its own code and is scored by its meta-utility on training tasks.
The starting improver in STOP: it asks a language model for several candidate improvements and returns the one with the best utility.
A task where a hidden rule says whether an odd number of chosen input bits are on, and the rule must be inferred from examples with some wrong labels.
A deterministic, seeded function used in a teaching script in place of a language model, so the output is reproducible.
The recorded chain of rewrites that produced a given improver, kept outside the improver so people can review each change.
The optimism that comes from picking the best of many noisy scores, because the winner's score includes luck as well as quality.
